note: Both sets cover the same core facts (Flexinol wire 15–30C transformation range, threaded base connection, 250 louvers, 32 aluminum rods, 3D ABS-printed pulley parts, CNC milling, design parameters) and both repeat the 32-rod, 250-louver and 15–30C facts under two names. B adds one well-supported claim A omits — rotational movement transferred via Kevlar strings to each pulley — while A adds nothing equivalent. Both turn bare diagram callout labels into unsupported 'connection' claims (idler pulley↔Kevlar string, Kevlar string↔Tension Spring) whose quotes are only the label text. B's only defect over A is a slightly altered quote ('cutting of each of the 250 louvers'), which does not change the claim.
remarks: Both sets treat the Screen Assembly Diagram callout labels (IDLER PULLEY, KEVLAR STRING, TENSION SPRING, NYLON BEARING SLEEVE, etc.) as component claims; the two 'connection' claims in each set are not supported by their quotes, which are only the label text. Both omit two of the four stated design parameters (allow cross ventilation, maintain privacy) and the hysteresis function of preventing continuous opening/closing cycles, and both omit the diagram parts FLEXINOL WIRE, ABS PULLEY WITH SET SCREW and THREADED TENSION CONTROL. Both duplicate the 32-rod, 250-louver and 15–30C facts under two entity names.
